analysis:
The PR changes only documentation. In docs/provider/cli-reference.md it adds one row at head line 1751 for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP in the daemon environment passthrough table. In docs/provider/direct-mode.md it rewrites the standalone preload paragraph (head lines 48-54) to say each preloaded model runs a load-time shape warmup. No source or security control is modified in the supplied evidence. Unit 32b0f686b2e810b1:0 is metadata only.

Checked the new passthrough row against the threat model. TB-003 and T-041 concern the prefix cache, attestation, App Attest authorization, fan helper and keys. The row adds a tuning knob that 0 disables warmup and 'always' skips its shader-cache probe. It touches no trust-boundary asset: no keys, tokens, attestation, authorization, cache scope, TTL or encryption. The warmup runs synthetic shapes and carries no consumer prompt data on the visible evidence.

The table's own heading says these variables are copied from the invoking shell into the LaunchAgent plist. That is unchanged behavior and an operator-only control, consistent with the existing passthrough entries. A local operator is already in the TB-003 threat model. The documented warmup and ModelCalibrationPolicy implementation are not supplied, so I cannot check that the warmup uses synthetic inputs only, or whether a warmup that persists compiled shader caches leaves any at-rest residue. This is an unverified contract for integration, not a finding.

The docs state a request arriving first preempts warmup. The scheduler code is not supplied, so it cannot be checked for availability impact (T-010, T-029). No finding is raised on this documentation-only change.
